title: Finite atomic support implies integrability
statement: Let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a measurable space with a finite measure, and let $X:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ be measurable. Suppose there is a finite set $s\subseteq\mathbb R$ such that $X$ lies in $s$ almost everywhere and, for every $x\in s$, $\mu(\{\omega:X(\omega)=x\})\ge\max(\lambda,0)$ for some $\lambda\in\mathbb R$. Then $X$ belongs to $L^p(\mu)$ for every extended nonnegative real exponent $p$.
hypotheses_covered: X is a measurable real-valued function
A finite set supports X almost everywhere
Each listed value has measure at least max(lambda, 0)
p is an extended nonnegative real exponent
replaced: Let $\mu$ be a finite measure and $X:\Omega\to\bbr$ measurable. If a finite set supports $X$ almost everywhere and each listed value has mass at least $\max(\lambda,0)$ for some real $\lambda$, then $X\in L^p(\mu)$ for every $p\in[0,\infty]$, including essential boundedness.
